rounds.text: The company is fundamentally outperforming its share price, evidenced by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 18% compared to a mere 2% price growth, alongside a massive 1318% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19, E21, E46]. Sales momentum is exceptionally strong, marked by a 31% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 5-year compounded sales growth of 33% [E15, E17]. Valuation metrics indicate mispricing, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 476 per share against the current market price of Rs 394, leaving a 17.3% margin of safety [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's price requires only a 15.4% growth rate, which is comfortably exceeded by the base case assumption of 18.0% and recent explosive earnings expansion [E21, E45]. The business generates real economic activity with Rs 44 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 16 Cr in free cash flow as of December 2025 [E35, E36], all while the committed promoter group maintains a rock-solid 74.97% stake [E40]. Conceded: the company carries a low return on equity, registering 4.1% and a median of 4% over the last year [E13, E29], and pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

The business suffers from exceptionally weak and chronically depressed returns on capital, highlighted by a 3-year median return on equity of just 3% [E28] and a low trailing return on equity of 4.1% [E13], severely lagging behind sector benchmarks where ROE sits at 13.49% [E9] and ROCE at 12.21% [E10]. This poor capital efficiency translates directly into poor shareholder wealth creation, evidenced by negative compounded share price growth of -11% over 3 years [E24] and -27% over 1 year [E25], alongside a complete lack of dividend payouts despite reported profits [E52]. Operational momentum is also deteriorating, marked by a compression in quarterly operating margins to 9% in September 2026 compared to 11% in the year-ago quarter [E31], rising borrowings reaching Rs 210 Cr in December 2025 [E38], and negative screen flags pointing to net profit dropping 8% year-over-year alongside decelerating earnings growth [E59, E60]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 1318% [E21] and a 5-year sales growth rate of 33% [E15].

While the bear highlights weak historical returns on capital such as a 3-year median ROE of 3% [E28] and a trailing ROE of 4.1% [E13], these figures ignore a massive structural acceleration where trailing twelve-month profit growth has surged by 1318% [E21] and 5-year sales compounded at 33% [E15]. Conceded: the bear correctly notes that the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4] and quarterly operating margins compressed by two percentage points to 9% in September 2026 [E31], but this operational margin pressure is completely overshadowed by robust cash generation, with operating cash flow hitting Rs 44 Cr and free cash flow reaching Rs 16 Cr by December 2025 [E35, E36]. Regarding the bear's concern over rising borrowings to Rs 210 Cr [E38], this capital structure supports a business that a discounted cash flow model explicitly values at Rs 476 per share against the current market price of Rs 394 [E43], leaving a clear 17.3% margin of safety [E44]. Furthermore, the bear's fixation on negative short-term share price performance like -27% over one year [E25] misses the fundamental reality that profit growth is vastly outpacing price momentum—specifically, 5-year profit growth of 18% [E19] dwarfs the meager 2% 5-year share price growth [E23], pointing to an undervalued asset where fundamentals are beginning to catch up to expectations [E46, E47].

Conceded: 5-year sales compounded at 33% [E15]. However, the bull's reliance on a massive 1318% TTV profit growth surge [E21] masks an earnings profile that is explicitly flagged as cyclical [E48], alongside screen warnings that net profit fell 8% YoY and earnings growth is decelerating [E59, E60]. While the bull points to operating and free cash flows of Rs 44 Cr and Rs 16 Cr respectively in December 2025 [E35, E36], borrowings concurrently ticked up to Rs 210 Cr [E38] while the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield and is explicitly flagged for its failure to distribute payouts despite repeated profits [E4, E52]. The bull cites a DCF value of Rs 476 [E43], but ignores that the rules-based screen only awards a neutral score of 51 out of 100 with medium confidence [E54], driven by severe underlying drags like low ROE of 4% [E61] and a 3-year share price contraction of -11% [E24]. Finally, the bull dismisses historical capital returns, yet the median ROE over 3 years sits at a dismal 3% [E28] and trailing ROE lingers at a low 4.1% [E13], confirming that structural underperformance outweighs short-term momentum arguments.
